newsitem.title: HUNGARY: STERLING AND DECEMBER BASKET DEALS HIGHLIGHT BCE.
newsitem.headline: STERLING AND DECEMBER BASKET DEALS HIGHLIGHT BCE.

text.p: The rising sterling, and basket deals for the December maturity were in focus in the Budapest Commodity Exchange's (BCE) currency futures market on Friday.
The sterling rose slightly for June and September, on what traders attributed to strengthening confidence in the U.K.'s economic policies and fundamentals.
"The sterling dropped four or five forints sometimes recently on news creating some uncertainty over the British economy, but it could always firm back," said Janos Szolyka of Swap brokerage.
The sterling closed at 300.40 forints for June and 310.70 for September.

The sterling accounted for 3,975 lots of the BCE currency futures turnover of 9,840 lots on Friday, while the second most active mark was traded in 3,900 lots of which the December maturity took out 3,600 lots.
Traders said basket deals for December were popular as they were less risky than other transactions.
Mark futures for December closed steady, while the dollar, which traded in 900 lots for December, finished at 196.00 forints, down 0.40 fillers for that maturity.
The Hungarian forint floats against a currency basket made up 30 percent of the dollar and 70 percent of the mark.
